body_markdown:
If your color looks a little muted, your roots feel oily by day two, or flakes show up right when you thought your routine was behaving, the question is simple: do you need a deeper cleanse, a dandruff shampoo, or both?


For color-treated hair with buildup and dandruff concerns, clarify no more than weekly. Many people should start with OLAPLEX Nº.4C Bond Maintenance Clarifying Shampoo every 1–2 weeks, or only when buildup signs return. If your flakes are dandruff-related, keep clarifying in its lane: it can help remove buildup, but a labeled dandruff shampoo is the flake-control step.


That rhythm gives your hair a reset without turning every wash day into a deep-clean day. Smart. Clean. Not overdone.


## **Start Here: How Often Should You Clarify?**


Use your hair’s behavior as the guide. Buildup has a way of announcing itself: hair looks dull, products stop spreading well, roots feel coated, or your usual shampoo leaves hair feeling not quite clean.


**What you notice** **A sensible starting cadence** **What to adjust**


Light styling product use, color-treated hair, no heavy oiliness


Every 1–2 weeks


Stretch longer if hair feels dry or color is fresh.


Regular dry shampoo, oils, heavy conditioners, or styling products


Up to weekly


Do not increase just because flakes appear; first decide whether flakes are buildup or dandruff-related.


Oily scalp plus visible buildup


Weekly as needed


If ends feel dry, focus your routine on the scalp and roots and give lengths more moisture in the rest of your routine.


Dry, fragile-feeling, vivid, fresh, or corrective color


Less often, only as needed


Wait at least two weeks after a color service before using Nº.4C, and check with your stylist.


Flakes that behave like dandruff


Clarify only for buildup


Use a dandruff shampoo as the flake-control step when dandruff is present.


The key is not to chase every scalp or color concern with the same shampoo. Clarifying is for residue. Dandruff care is for dandruff. Color care is about timing and restraint.


## **Buildup Versus Dandruff: Your Routine Has Two Jobs**


Product buildup is residue. It can come from styling products, oils, dry shampoo, minerals, or richer conditioners that leave hair feeling coated. When buildup is the problem, hair may feel heavy, look flat at the roots, lose shine, or seem resistant to your usual products.


Dandruff-related flaking is different. It is a scalp concern, not simply styling residue sitting on the hair. That is why a clarifying shampoo should not be treated as a dandruff treatment. Clarifying can help reset hair and scalp when buildup is in the way; dandruff shampoo is the flake-control step when dandruff is present.


A practical way to decide:


-


If flakes show up with dull, coated, product-heavy hair, buildup may be part of the picture.


-


If flakes keep returning even when your hair feels clean, dandruff may need its own routine.


-


If clarifying makes flakes look worse or your scalp feels less comfortable, do not clarify more often. Pull back and treat that as a sign the issue may not be buildup alone.


Clean hair is the goal. Over-cleansed hair is not the plot.


## **How to Clarify Around Color Without Overdoing It**


Color-treated hair can benefit from a reset when buildup makes color look muted. The trick is timing.


Wait at least two weeks after a color service before using OLAPLEX Nº.4C. If your color is vivid, fragile, corrective, or freshly toned, check with your stylist before clarifying. Your color history matters, and your stylist knows the work that went into it.


Once you are past that fresh-color window, keep the cadence conservative. Weekly can make sense when buildup is clear and recurring. Every 1–2 weeks is a better starting point for many routines. If hair starts to feel dry, color is newly refreshed, or flakes worsen after clarifying, stretch the time between clarifying washes.


Over-washing and unnecessary deep cleansing can work against the polished, color-fresh finish you are trying to keep. Think of clarifying as a reset button, not your default button.


## **Where OLAPLEX Nº.4C Fits In Your Routine**


Use OLAPLEX Nº.4C when buildup is the problem you want to solve. It is our weekly, pH-optimised clarifying shampoo for all hair types and textures, designed to deeply cleanse and remove damaging buildup from the scalp and hair while helping restore color vibrancy, shine, and softness.\[1\]


It is also designed to cleanse without stripping, helping restore color vibrancy, shine, and softness.\[1\] For color-treated hair, that combination matters: you want the coated feeling gone, not your hair left feeling rough, dry, or flat.


Here is the clean fit:


**Routine question** **How Nº.4C fits**


What is it for?


A buildup-reset wash for hair that feels coated, dull, heavy, or less responsive to products.


How often should I use it?


Weekly as needed, or every 1–2 weeks as a cautious starting point.


Who can use it?


It is for all hair types and textures.\[1\]


What does it help with?


It removes buildup and helps restore color vibrancy, shine, and softness.\[1\]


What is it not?


It is not a dandruff treatment. Use a dandruff shampoo as the flake-control step when dandruff is present.


What about fresh color?


Wait at least two weeks after a color service before using Nº.4C, and check with your stylist for vivid, fragile, or corrective color.


Nº.4C is made for the moment when hair needs a true clean slate. It effectively removes buildup without stripping or drying hair or impacting color.\[1\] It also provides a deep cleanse at a surface level without stripping essential moisture.\[1\]


If your broader routine focuses on repair, Nº.4C can also help maximize the efficacy of a hair repair routine by clearing the way for the rest of your wash-care steps.\[1\] That is the role: reset first, then let the rest of your routine do its work.


## **How Claims Are Supported**


We keep product claims and scalp-care guidance separate because they answer different questions.


The Nº.4C statements in this article are based on our official product information: pH-optimised clarifying care, use for all hair types and textures, buildup removal, color vibrancy, shine, softness, and non-stripping cleansing.\[1\] Claims are based on scientific research and professional use.


Guidance about dandruff stays more cautious. Clarifying shampoo can help remove buildup, but when dandruff is present, a dandruff shampoo is the appropriate flake-control step. Nº.4C should not be used or described as a treatment for dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis, fungus, itching, redness, irritation, or scalp disease.


That distinction keeps your routine clear: cleanse what is coating the hair, and choose a dandruff-focused step when flakes are the issue.


## **FAQ**


### **Can I use clarifying shampoo instead of dandruff shampoo?**


No. Use clarifying shampoo for buildup, not as a replacement for dandruff shampoo. If dandruff is present, a dandruff shampoo is the flake-control step; a clarifying shampoo can still be used separately when residue, oil, dry shampoo, minerals, or heavy conditioners are making hair feel coated.


### **What if my flakes get worse after clarifying?**


Stop increasing your clarifying frequency. Worsening flakes can be a sign that buildup is not the only issue, or that your current cadence is too much for your scalp and hair. Stretch the time between clarifying washes and keep dandruff care separate from your buildup-reset step.


### **Is OLAPLEX Nº.4C safe for permanent color?**


Nº.4C is designed to remove buildup without stripping or drying hair or impacting color.\[1\] For timing, wait at least two weeks after a color service before using it, and check with your stylist if your color is vivid, fragile, corrective, or freshly refreshed.


### **Can dry shampoo replace clarifying shampoo?**


No. Dry shampoo can help absorb oil between washes, but it does not replace cleansing. If dry shampoo is part of your routine, it can also be one of the residues that makes a clarifying wash useful when hair starts to feel coated or dull.


## **The Polished Takeaway**


Clarify when your hair is asking for a reset, not every time your scalp or color has a concern. For many color-treated routines, every 1–2 weeks is the right place to start; weekly can work when buildup is clear and recurring. Keep dandruff shampoo in the routine when dandruff is present, and give fresh color at least two weeks before your first Nº.4C wash.


When buildup is the issue, OLAPLEX Nº.4C is the clean, focused reset: a pH-optimised clarifying shampoo for all hair types and textures that helps restore color vibrancy, shine, and softness while removing damaging buildup from the scalp and hair.\[1\] Use it with intention, keep the cadence calm, and let your hair get back to looking like it has plans.
